class.peasant.family.MAY: into a family of milpa farmers
class.landowner.family.MAY: into the family of a sajal, a lord of the court
class.noble.family.MAY: into the royal lineage of the ajaws
prof.farmer.desc.MAY: Clear and burn the forest, plant maize, beans and squash - and pray to Chaak for rain.
prof.laborer.desc.MAY: There are no pack animals and no wheels here: stone, lime and goods are carried on people’s backs.
prof.artisan.desc.MAY: Painted pottery, figurines, flint and obsidian tools - the city lives by your hands.
prof.weaver.desc.MAY: You spin cotton and weave on a backstrap loom. Cotton mantles are clothing, tribute and money all at once.
prof.midwife.desc.MAY: You help at births and know the herbs and the prayers to the goddess Ix Chel.
prof.merchant.desc.MAY: Jade, obsidian, salt, cacao and quetzal feathers pass from hand to hand across the whole Maya world.
prof.sailor.desc.MAY: Dugout canoes carry salt and cacao along the Usumacinta and its tributaries. The rapids forgive no mistakes.
prof.soldier.desc.MAY: Spear, flint knife and shield. The greatest glory is to bring back a captive.
prof.scribe.desc.MAY: You write glyphs on vessels, walls and bark-paper books. Only a handful of people in a whole city can write.
prof.physician.desc.MAY: Herbs, bloodletting, spells and the count of days: illness is both the body and the anger of the gods.
prof.priest.desc.MAY: You keep the sacred calendar, choose the lucky days and speak to the gods for the people.
prof.landholder.desc.MAY: Farmers of several villages work for you, and you answer to the court for their tribute.
prof.magistrate.desc.MAY: You rule a subject town in the name of the holy lord: justice, tribute, warriors and the dangerous closeness of the throne.
prof.matron.as.MAY: the lady of a noble house
prof.matron.desc.MAY: Servants, weavers, stores, feasts and alliances between families - all of it rests on you.
prof.household_slave.desc.MAY: You were taken in war or sold for debt. Now you carry water and grind maize in someone else’s house.
prof.field_slave.desc.MAY: Hard labour in your master’s milpas and on his building sites.
prof.officer.desc.MAY: You lead a band on raids, and you answer for every captive taken and every man lost.
prof.workshop_owner.desc.MAY: Your own workshop, apprentices and orders from the court itself.
prof.official.MAY: Aj k'uhuun, keeper of the sacred books
prof.official.as.MAY: an aj k'uhuun, a keeper of the sacred books
prof.official.desc.MAY: A court post: the books, the tribute, the tally of captives and festivals.
prof.overseer.desc.MAY: A captive whom the master has trusted with other captives and with his fields.
prof.ballplayer.desc: Pitz is the game of the gods: you strike a heavy rubber ball with your hip. Fame, noble wagers - and broken ribs.
prof.jade_carver.desc: Jade is harder than any blade: you grind it with sand and water for weeks. Your beads and masks go to palaces and tombs.
prof.stone_carver.desc: You carve stelae, altars and the faces of kings. The scribe draws - you cut.
prof.feather_worker.desc: You turn quetzal, macaw and heron feathers into headdresses, fans and dance regalia.
place.may_puuc: the Puuc hills in the north
place.may_forest_hamlet: a hamlet deep in the forest
lifestyle.food.plain.desc.MAY: Maize gruel, tamales, beans, squash and chili
lifestyle.food.varied.desc.MAY: Venison, turkey, fish, fruit, cacao. Good for your health
lifestyle.food.feasts.desc.MAY: Feasts with frothy cacao and balché, guests and fame. Expensive
lifestyle.exercise.gymnasium.desc.MAY: Practice on the ballcourt and hunting in the forest. Stronger and healthier
lifestyle.medicine.home.desc.MAY: Herbs, brews and the neighbours’ advice
lifestyle.medicine.temple.desc.MAY: The aj k’in counts the days, names the god to blame and says what to offer
lifestyle.medicine.physician.desc.MAY: A healer treats the whole family with herbs and bloodletting. Expensive, but fewer die
lifestyle.baths.rarely.desc.MAY: A stream and a gourd of water
lifestyle.baths.daily.desc.MAY: The pibnaah sweatbath every day: steam, herbs, talk. You must live in the city
focus.learn.desc.MAY: Learn numbers and glyphs from a scribe. It is rare and costly knowledge
focus.study.desc.MAY: Glyphs, the calendar, the stars and the words of the ancestors. Costly
focus.service.desc.MAY: Spear practice and raids on neighbours
ev.found_coin.text.MAY: By the road you found a dropped pouch of cacao beans. No one saw.
ev.school_offer.text.MAY: A scribe the family knows will teach you to count in dots and bars and to read your first glyphs. He must be paid in cacao, and your help at home is needed right now.
ev.child_school.text.MAY: The child has grown. You could send them to study with a scribe or a priest - or keep them at home to help.
ev.festival.text.MAY: A period-ending festival: a new stela rises in the plaza, priests burn copal, and the nobles dance in masks and feathers. In the evening everyone is fed tamales.
ev.a_debtor_saves.text.MAY: On a deserted forest path robbers surrounded you - and then around the bend came the porter whose debt you once forgave, with his three sons carrying spears. The robbers scattered.
ev.t_friend_returns.text.MAY: The one you once stood surety for has come back - grey-haired, in a fine cotton mantle. He stands at your door with a sack of cacao and cannot raise his eyes. "I grew rich in far-off lands. Here is everything I owe you, and more."
ev.t_friend_returns.take.ok.MAY: You counted the beans in front of him. Every one. The debt is closed - and nothing more.
ev.t_friend_returns.forgive.ok.MAY: You sat until morning over balché, remembering your youth. Not every friendship can be saved, but this one was.
ev.t_friend_returns.drive_away.ok.MAY: You let the door mat fall without taking a single bean. Pride is wealth too.
ev.v_wine_liver.text.MAY: The whites of your eyes have turned yellow, your belly is swollen, and in the mornings the nausea keeps you down. The healer pressed your side for a long time and finally said it plainly: it is the balché.
ev.v_wine_liver.quit.success.MAY: Fear proved stronger than the craving. The yellow took months to fade, but you never touched balché again.
ev.v_wine_liver.quit.failure.MAY: You lasted a week. Your body called for balché louder than the healer’s warnings.
ev.v_wine_liver.treat.ok.MAY: The healer took the cacao and only sighed. You felt better - until the next rainy season.
ev.y_runaway_thanks.text.MAY: At the landing a weather-beaten man came up to you. "Don’t you know me? The storeroom, the tamales, the night. You didn’t give me away. I got out - and now I paddle trading canoes, far from here, where no one is looking for me."
ev.y_runaway_thanks.friendship.MAY: Invite him for a cup of balché
prof.salt_trader.desc.MAY: Salt from the coast is needed by every household in the forest. Long roads, heavy baskets and good money.
